readerTitle: The yoga studio that didn't need more ads
caseNote: 가상 사례 (요가 스튜디오, 동네 찻집) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 성장 계획은 광고 예산이 아니라 고객이 가장 많이 빠져나가는 단계와 사람들이 이야기할 거리에서 시작한다.
misconception: 회원이 안 늘면 광고를 더 하면 된다. 입소문은 돈을 주고 부탁해야 생긴다.

sources.text: 모든 수치와 사례는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 가상입니다. 현재 흐름: 첫 수업 50명 → 두 번째 수업 20명(40%) → 가입 15명(재방문자의 75%) → 해지 12명(회원 120명 × 10%) → 순증 +3명.
요가 스튜디오 업계의 실제 체험 전환율이나 해지율은 인용하지 않았습니다. 카드 수치를 업계 평균처럼 표현하지 않도록 확인하세요.

cards.title: The yoga studio that didn't need more ads
body: Maya runs a small yoga studio with 120 members. Every month, new people walk in. Every month, the member count barely moves.
She's about to spend $1,500 a month on online ads. Before she does, let's look at where people go.

image.label: Yoga studio door with people walking in and quietly leaving
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 작은 요가 스튜디오 정문으로 사람들이 줄지어 들어오지만, 옆문으로 비슷한 수가 조용히 나가는 장면. 실제 브랜드 로고나 간판은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Follow 50 first-timers.
body: The biggest drop isn't at the door. It's **after the first class**: 30 of 50 never come back.

breakdown.label: First class
breakdown.detail: People who try an intro class

cards.title: Where should Maya put her effort first?
body: She has $1,500 a month and a few hours of her teachers' time. Which move grows the studio most?

options.text: Run the ads to bring in about 20 more first-timers a month
options.feedback: More acquisition helps, but 60% of the new people would still leave after one class. You'd pay to fill a leaky bucket.

options.text: Make sure first-timers book a second class before they leave
options.feedback: This fixes activation, the step where most people drop. It costs little, and every future visitor benefits from it.

options.text: Offer members 20% off to stop them cancelling
options.feedback: Retention matters, but a discount cuts what every member pays, including those who'd have stayed anyway. It also skips the bigger leak.

cards.title: Fixing one step beats buying more traffic.
body: If 60% come back instead of 40%, that's 30 returners and about 22 new members. Net growth jumps from +3 to **+10 a month**, for almost no cost.
The ads would bring 70 first-timers, 28 returners and 21 new members. That's +9, for $1,500 a month.
Maya's fix: teachers learn each newcomer's name, help them book a second class at the desk, and send a short message the next day.
cards.softwareNote: In an app, the same leak sits between sign-up and the second session. Ads poured into weak activation buy users who disappear within a week.

cards.title: Now Maya wants members to spread the word.
body: Most of her loyal members first came because a friend mentioned the studio. She wants more of that. What should she try?

options.text: Pay members $20 for each friend who joins
options.feedback: A reward can work, but it's a referral program, not word of mouth. It pays for sign-ups without giving people anything new to talk about.

options.text: Start a free Saturday class in the park that members can bring friends to
options.feedback: This creates word of mouth: an easy, social reason to mention the studio and a low-risk way for friends to try it.

options.text: Give a free class for every five-star online review
options.feedback: You may get more stars, but paid praise reads as paid. It can also break review site rules and erode trust.

cards.title: People talk when you give them a story and an invitation.
body: **Word of mouth** grows when customers have something worth mentioning and an easy way to bring someone along.
A class in the park is visible and a little unusual. Inviting a friend feels like sharing a nice Saturday, not making a sales pitch.
And the friend arrives with someone they know, which makes a second visit more likely. Word of mouth and activation help each other.

image.label: Outdoor yoga class with members and their friends
image.brief: 공원 잔디밭의 토요일 아침 요가 수업. 매트 몇 개는 짝을 지어 놓여 있어 회원이 친구를 데려온 느낌. 밝고 친근한 톤, 로고 없음.

cards.title: Word of mouth spreads whatever is true.
body: If newcomers still feel ignored after the first class, more visitors just means more people saying "it was fine." Fix the leak before you turn up the volume.
Small numbers also swing a lot. One good month with 50 people can be luck. Watch a few months before deciding a change worked.

cards.title: Now it's a neighborhood tea shop.
body: Plenty of people buy a first bag of loose-leaf tea. Few come back. The owner is pricing a flyer campaign for the whole neighborhood. What would you do first?

options.text: Print the flyers to bring in more first-time buyers
options.feedback: That's acquisition into the same leak. Most new buyers would still make one purchase and drift away.

options.text: Give first-time buyers a brewing card and an invite to a monthly tasting they can bring a friend to
options.feedback: The card fixes activation, so the first tea tastes right at home. The tasting gives people a reason to come back and to talk.

options.text: Start a stamp card: the tenth bag free
options.feedback: It rewards retention, but only for people who already return. Most buyers never reach stamp two.

cards.title: Find the leak, then give people something to share.
body: This lesson used **acquisition, activation and retention** to find where customers drop, and **word of mouth** to grow without paying for every visitor.
**Try it today:** count how many new customers you had last month and how many came back a second time. Which step loses the most people?
